value of inventories to their cost on an aggregate basis, excluding materials and supplies. In determining the market value of our inventories, we assume that feedstocks are converted into refined products, which requires us to make estimates regarding the refined products expected to be produced from those feedstocks and the conversion costs required to convert those feedstocks into refined products. We also estimate the usual and customary transportation costs required to move the inventory from our plants to the appropriate points of sale. We then apply an estimated selling price to our inventories. If the aggregate market value is less than the aggregate cost, we recognize a loss for the difference in our statements of income. However, to the extent the aggregate market value subsequently increases, we would recognize an increase to the value of our inventories (not to exceed cost) and a gain in our statements of income.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The market value of our last-in, first-out (LIFO) inventory as of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> fell below our historical LIFO inventory costs. Therefore, our income tax rate for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> is our best estimate of our annual effective income tax rate.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">CARES Act</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">On March&#160;27, 2020, the Coronavirus Aid, Relief and Economic Security (CARES) Act was enacted, which resulted in significant changes to the U.S. Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. This provision allows the taxpayer to recover taxes previously paid at a </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">35</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;percent federal income tax rate during tax years prior to 2018. Also, a taxpayer can elect to use its 2019 adjusted taxable income in 2020 to determine the deductible amount of interest expense in that year.</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We recognized an overall income tax benefit of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$<ix:nonFraction id="d13666549e615-wk-Fact-76D48B4587335E96A869830C6982D918" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxExpenseBenefit" contextRef="FD2020Q1YTD" unitRef="usd" decimals="-6" scale="6" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">616</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, of which </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$<ix:nonFraction id="d13666549e627-wk-Fact-CD7B731C9A7043F46E8E99A20C49C88E" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxReconciliationChangeInEnactedTaxRate" contextRef="FD2020Q1YTD" unitRef="usd" decimals="-6" scale="6" sign="-" format="ixt:numdotdecimal">110</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> was attributable to the expected tax NOL carryback provided for under the CARES Act for expected tax NOLs from our current tax year to our 2015 income tax year in which we paid federal income tax at a </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">35</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;percent tax rate. The liability for environmental credits is based on our deficit for such credits as of the balance sheet date, if any, after considering any credits acquired or under contract, and is equal to the product of the credits deficit and the market price of these credits as of the balance sheet date. The environmental credit obligations are categorized in Level&#160;2 of the fair value hierarchy and are measured at fair value using a market approach based on quoted prices from an independent Some of these contracts are derivative instruments; however, we elect the normal purchase exception and do not record these contracts at their fair values. Certain of these programs require us to blend biofuels into the products we produce, and we are subject to such programs in most of the countries in which we operate. These non-GAAP financial measures include adjusted operating income (including adjusted operating income for each of our reportable segments, as applicable) and refining, renewable diesel, and ethanol segment margin. We have included these non-GAAP financial measures to help facilitate the comparison of operating results between periods. See the tables in note&#160;(c) beginning on page&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">41</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for reconciliations of these non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable U.S. GAAP financial measures. Also in note&#160;(c), we disclose the reasons why we believe our use of the non-GAAP financial measures provides useful information.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div><a id="s08F9502E6D9D5489B350B3CD12790535"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">OVERVIEW AND OUTLOOK</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div><a id="sD9AC6B3681735F9EAC124D25EBC04924"></a></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Overview</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Business Operations Update</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The recent outbreak of COVID-19 and its development into a pandemic in March 2020 has resulted in significant economic disruption globally, including in North America and Europe, the primary geographic areas where we operate. Governmental authorities around the world have taken actions, such as stay-at-home orders and other social distancing measures, to prevent the spread of COVID-19 that has restricted travel, public gatherings, and the overall level of individual movement and in-person interaction across the globe.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">This has, in turn, significantly reduced global economic activity and negatively impacted many businesses. Airlines have dramatically reduced flights and motor vehicle usage has significantly declined at a time when seasonal driving patterns typically result in an increase of consumer demand for gasoline. As a result, there has also been a decline in the demand for, and thus also the market prices of, crude oil, and most of our products, particularly gasoline, jet fuel, and ethanol. In addition, global crude oil production levels have not declined despite lower demand and storage capacity constraints for crude oil and refined products, which has exacerbated the decline in crude oil prices and has contributed to an increase in crude oil price volatility.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The decrease in the demand for refined petroleum products coupled with the decline in the price of crude oil has resulted in a significant decrease in the price of refined petroleum products manufactured by our refining segment. For example, the price of gasoline</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(a)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in the U.S. Gulf Coast region where eight of our 15&#160;refineries are located was $68.82&#160;per barrel at the beginning of 2020, fell to $58.84&#160;per barrel by the beginning of March, and was $17.65&#160;per barrel at the end of March. This represents a 74&#160;percent decline during the first quarter with most of that decline occurring in the latter half of March as travel and related restrictions started to impact demand for gasoline and as crude oil prices declined. Another example is the price of diesel</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(b)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in the U.S. Gulf Coast region, which was $81.71&#160;per barrel at the beginning of 2020, fell to $62.10&#160;per barrel by the beginning of March, and was $39.18&#160;per barrel at the end of March. This represents a 52&#160;percent decline during the first quarter. The decrease in the price of diesel was not as significant as the decrease in the price of gasoline because it is the primary fuel used by industry and essential businesses, including the critical logistics infrastructure to move and transport goods produced by those businesses. On April&#160;28, 2020, the price of gasoline</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(a)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> had improved to $22.74&#160;per barrel, but the price of diesel</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(b)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> had declined to $23.21&#160;per barrel as a result of decreased demand.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">34</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;" href="#s7AFF93F8504350BE9A3C9FED6360EC70"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The price of ethanol manufactured by our ethanol segment has also decreased due to a decline in demand. Because ethanol is primarily blended into gasoline, ethanol demand has declined along with the decline in the demand for gasoline. Demand for renewable diesel is consistent with the demand for diesel as a whole; therefore, our renewable diesel segment has not been impacted as significantly as our refining and ethanol segments.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Prices for the products we sell and the feedstocks we purchase impact our revenues, cost of sales, operating income, and liquidity. In addition, a decline in the market prices of products and feedstocks below their carrying values in our inventory results in a writedown in the value of our inventories. For the first quarter of 2020, we generated an operating loss of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.3&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, which includes a </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.5&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> loss in the value of our inventories. Our operating results for the first quarter of 2020, including operating results by segment, are described in the summary below and detailed descriptions can be found under &#8220;RESULTS OF OPERATIONS&#8221; on pages&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">38 </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">through </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">48</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Our liquidity has also been impacted by the decline in the market prices for our products because the amount of cash generated by our product sales has declined more rapidly than the amount of cash used to pay for our crude oil purchases. While this relationship is not abnormal or unusual in our business where daily product sales follow the market prices on that day, the negative impact on our cash position is more significant when the market prices decline rapidly as they did in the latter half of March. For the first quarter of 2020, net cash used by our operating activities was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$49&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, which was negatively impacted by an </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$825&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> use of cash</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(c)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> as a result of rapidly falling market prices. Overall, our cash and cash equivalents declined by </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$1.1&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> during the first quarter of 2020, from </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$2.6&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> as of December&#160;31, 2019 to </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$1.5&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> as of March&#160;31, 2020. In addition to the net use of cash by our operating activities, we invested </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$705&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> in our business and returned </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">$548&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> to our stockholders through dividends and purchases of our common stock. Even though our cash and cash equivalents on hand declined during the first quarter of 2020, we ended the quarter with </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">$6.3&#160;billion</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of liquidity</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:7pt">(d)</sup></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. A summary of our cash flows is presented on page&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">50</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, and a description of our cash flows and other matters impacting our liquidity and capital resources, including measures we have taken or are considering to take, can be found under &#8220;LIQUIDITY AND CAPITAL RESOURCES&#8221; on pages&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">49</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> through&#160;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">52</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We are actively responding to the impacts from these matters on our business. We have reduced the amount of crude oil processed at most of our refineries in response to the decreased demand for our products, we have temporarily idled various gasoline-making units at certain of our refineries to further limit gasoline production, and we have taken measures to reduce jet fuel production. Eight of our ethanol plants are temporarily idled, and we reduced the amount of ethanol produced at our remaining six ethanol plants to address the decreased demand for ethanol. In addition to these measures, we have addressed our liquidity as outlined below:</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-bottom:0px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:60px;"></td><td></td></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:36px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We deferred projects representing approximately </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;text-align:right;vertical-align:bottom;">$400&#160;million</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of capital investments that we had expected to make in 2020 related to our refining and ethanol segments.</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:0px;text-align:justify;padding-left:60px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-bottom:0px;font-family:Times New Roman; The market prices for refined petroleum products generally track the price of benchmark crude oils, such as Brent, WTI, and ANS; therefore, our refining segment margin is affected by our ability to purchase and process crude oils and other feedstocks that are priced at a discount to the benchmark crude oils. While we benefit when we process these types of crude oils and other feedstocks, that benefit will vary as the discount widens or narrows. Improvement in these discounts has a favorable impact on our refining segment margin as it lowers our cost of materials; whereas lower discounts result in higher cost of materials, which has a negative impact on our refining segment margin. Actual results could differ from those estimates. Our critical accounting estimates are included in our annual report on Form&#160;10-K for the year ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. As of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the following accounting policy is included as it involves estimates that are considered critical due to the level of subjectivity and judgment involved, as well as the impact on our financial position and results of operations. We believe that all of our estimates are reasonable. Estimates of the sensitivity to earnings that would result from changes in the assumptions used in determining our estimates are not practicable due to the number of assumptions and contingencies involved, and the wide range of possible outcomes.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Impairment of Long-Lived Assets and Goodwill</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Long-lived assets are tested for recoverability whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of the asset may not be recoverable. A long-lived asset is not recoverable if its carrying amount exceeds the sum of the undiscounted cash flows expected to result from its use and eventual disposition. If a long-lived asset is not recoverable, an impairment loss is recognized for the amount by which the carrying amount of the long-lived asset exceeds its fair value, with fair value determined based on discounted estimated net cash flows or other appropriate methods.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Goodwill is tested for impairment annually or more frequently if events or changes in circumstances indicate the asset might be impaired. An impairment loss is recognized if the carrying amount of the asset exceeds its fair value.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">As of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, we completed an impairment analysis of certain of our long-lived assets and goodwill and determined they were not impaired, as discussed in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;2</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of Condensed Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div><br/></div><div style="text-align:center;"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">54</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"></hr><div><a id="s3978AFDC5D46509CAF8B1830F5845797"></a></div><div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"><a style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;" href="#s7AFF93F8504350BE9A3C9FED6360EC70"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:8pt;color:#0000ff;">Table of Contents</span></a></div></div><div><br/></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; <tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The entire disclosure for the fair value of financial instruments (as defined), including financial assets and financial liabilities (collectively, as defined), and the measurements of those instruments as well as disclosures related to the fair value of non-financial assets and liabilities. Such disclosures about the financial instruments, assets, and liabilities would include: (1) the fair value of the required items together with their carrying amounts (as appropriate); (2) for items for which it is not practicable to estimate fair value, disclosure would include: (a) information pertinent to estimating fair value (including, carrying amount, effective interest rate, and maturity, and (b) the reasons why it is not practicable to estimate fair value; (3) significant concentrations of credit risk including: (a) information about the activity, region, or economic characteristics identifying a concentration, (b) the maximum amount of loss the entity is exposed to based on the gross fair value of the related item, (c) policy for requiring collateral or other security and information as to accessing such collateral or security, and (d) the nature and brief description of such collateral or security; (4) quantitative information about market risks and how such risks are managed; (5) for items measured on both a recurring and nonrecurring basis information regarding the inputs used to develop the fair value measurement; and (6) for items presented in the financial statement for which fair value measurement is elected: (a) information necessary to understand the reasons for the election, (b) discussion of the effect of fair value changes on earnings, (c) a description of [similar groups] items for which the election is made and the relation thereof to the balance sheet, the aggregate carrying value of items included in the balance sheet that are not eligible for the election; (7) all other required (as defined) and desired information.</p></div>

<table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_ExciseAndSalesTaxes">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>The amount of excise and sales taxes included in sales and revenues, which are then deducted as a cost of sales. Includes excise taxes, which are applied to specific types of transactions or items (such as gasoline or alcohol); and sales, use and value added taxes, which are applied to a broad class of revenue-producing transactions involving a wide range of goods and services.</p></div>

<th class="th" colspan="1">3 Months Ended</th>

<tr><th class="th"><div>Mar. 31, 2020</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_RisksAndUncertaintiesAbstract', window );"><strong>Risks and Uncertainties [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl custom" style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_vlo_UncertaintiesandSignificantAccountingEstimatesDisclosureTextBlock', window );">UNCERTAINTIES AND CERTAIN SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:0px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">2.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">UNCERTAINTIES AND CERTAIN SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Overview</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The outbreak of COVID-19 and its development into a pandemic in March&#160;2020 and certain developments in the global oil markets have impacted and continue to impact our business. We are actively responding to these matters on our business. We have reduced the amount of crude oil processed at most of our refineries in response to the decreased demand for our products, we have temporarily idled various gasoline-making units at certain of our refineries to further limit gasoline production, and we have taken measures to reduce jet fuel production. </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>Eight</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of our ethanol plants are temporarily idled, and we reduced the amount of ethanol produced at our remaining </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>six</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> ethanol plants to address the decreased demand for ethanol.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Many uncertainties remain with respect to COVID-19, including its resulting economic effects, and we are unable to predict the ultimate economic impacts from COVID-19 on our business and how quickly national economies can recover once the pandemic subsides. However, the adverse impacts of the economic effects from COVID-19 and uncertainty in the global oil markets on our business have been and will likely continue to be significant. As a result, we expect these matters may affect our estimates and assumptions on amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes in the near term.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Impairment Analysis of Long-Lived Assets</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Due to the adverse economic conditions discussed above, we reviewed our significant operating assets for the existence of impairment indicators. As a result of this review, we evaluated </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>six</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;ethanol plants for potential impairment as of March&#160;31, 2020, assuming that we would operate these plants in the future and incorporating current price assumptions into our future estimated cash flows. Based on our analysis, we determined that </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">the carrying amount of each of these plants was recoverable, as the undiscounted future cash flows from each plant exceeded its respective carrying value. Nonetheless, we will continue to evaluate the economic conditions and their impact on our assumptions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Impairment Analysis of Goodwill</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We have </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$260&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of goodwill as of March&#160;31, 2020. All of our goodwill is allocated to one reporting unit, the U.S. Gulf Coast refining region. Our annual test for the impairment of goodwill is performed on October&#160;1 of each year. However, as discussed above, there were adverse changes in the capital and commodity markets that contributed to a significant decline in our common stock price. Despite the decline in our common stock price, we determined our goodwill was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>no</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">t impaired. Nonetheless, we will continue to evaluate the economic conditions and their impact on our assumptions.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Inventory Valuation</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">See </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;4</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> regarding our </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$2.5&#160;billion</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> LCM inventory valuation reserve and the estimates used to determine the market value of our inventories.</span></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Mar. 31, 2020</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_IncomeTaxDisclosureAbstract', window );"><strong>Income Tax Disclosure [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_IncomeTaxDisclosureTextBlock', window );">INCOME TAXES</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:0px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">10.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">INCOME TAXES</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Determination of Quarterly Effective Income Tax Rate</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We have historically calculated the provision for income taxes during interim reporting periods by applying an estimate of the annual effective tax rate for the full year to income for the interim period. Given the significant uncertainty with respect to the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak on our business and results of operations, we are not currently able to estimate our annual effective income tax rate for 2020. Therefore, our income tax rate for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> is our best estimate of our annual effective income tax rate.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">CARES Act</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">On March&#160;27, 2020, the Coronavirus Aid, Relief and Economic Security (CARES) Act was enacted, which resulted in significant changes to the U.S. Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. The most significant changes affecting us were as follows:</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:48px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Modification of the limitations previously set by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 by providing that tax net operating losses (NOLs) arising in a tax year beginning in 2018, 2019, or 2020 can be carried back five years. This provision allows the taxpayer to recover taxes previously paid at a </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">35</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;percent federal income tax rate during tax years prior to 2018. In addition, the CARES Act removed the taxable income limitation to allow a tax NOL to fully offset taxable income for tax years beginning before January&#160;1, 2021.</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:48px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Increased the deductibility of interest expense from </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">30</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;percent to </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">50</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;percent of adjusted taxable income for 2019 and 2020. Also, a taxpayer can elect to use its 2019 adjusted taxable income in 2020 to determine the deductible amount of interest expense in that year.</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We recognized an overall income tax benefit of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$616&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, of which </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$110&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> was attributable to the expected tax NOL carryback provided for under the CARES Act for expected tax NOLs from our current tax year to our 2015 income tax year in which we paid federal income tax at a </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">35</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;percent tax rate. In addition, we were not limited in the amount of interest expense we could deduct. The remaining income tax benefit was primarily due to the LCM inventory valuation adjustment that resulted in a tax benefit of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$551&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<th class="th" colspan="1">3 Months Ended</th>

<tr><th class="th"><div>Mar. 31, 2020</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_BusinessCombinationsAbstract', window );"><strong>Business Combinations [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>

<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock', window );">MERGER WITH VLP</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:0px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">3.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">MERGER WITH VLP</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">On January&#160;10, 2019, we completed our acquisition of all of the outstanding publicly held common units of VLP pursuant to a definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger (Merger Agreement, and together with the transactions contemplated thereby, the Merger Transaction) with VLP. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, each outstanding publicly held common unit was converted into the right to receive </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$42.25</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#160;per common unit in cash without any interest thereon, and all such publicly traded common units were automatically canceled and ceased to exist. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, we paid aggregate merger consideration of</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$950&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, which was funded with available cash on hand.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Prior to the completion of the Merger Transaction, we consolidated the financial statements of VLP and reflected noncontrolling interests on our balance sheet for the portion of VLP&#8217;s partners&#8217; capital held by VLP&#8217;s public common unitholders. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, VLP became our indirect wholly owned subsidiary and, as a result, we no longer reflect noncontrolling interests on our balance sheet with respect to VLP. In addition, we no longer attribute a portion of VLP&#8217;s net income to noncontrolling interests. Because we had a controlling financial interest in VLP before the Merger Transaction and retained our controlling financial interest in VLP after the Merger Transaction, the change in our ownership interest in VLP as a result of the merger was accounted for as an equity transaction. Accordingly, we did not recognize a gain or loss on the Merger Transaction.</span></div><span></span>
</td>
</tr>

<th class="tl" colspan="1" rowspan="2"><div style="width: 200px;"><strong>Price Risk Management Activities<br></strong></div></th>
<th class="th" colspan="1">3 Months Ended</th>
</tr>
<tr><th class="th"><div>Mar. 31, 2020</div></th></tr>
<tr class="re">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureAbstract', window );"><strong>Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities Disclosure [Abstract]</strong></a></td>
<td class="text">&#160;<span></span>
</td>
</tr>
<tr class="ro">
<td class="pl " style="border-bottom: 0px;" valign="top"><a class="a" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.showAR( this, 'defref_us-gaap_DerivativeInstrumentsAndHedgingActivitiesDisclosureTextBlock', window );">PRICE RISK MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES</a></td>
<td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:0px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">15.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">PRICE RISK MANAGEMENT ACTIVITIES</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:24px;text-indent:-24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">General</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We are exposed to market risks primarily related to the volatility in the price of commodities, foreign currency exchange rates, and the price of credits needed to comply with various government and regulatory programs. We enter into derivative instruments to manage some of these risks, including derivative instruments related to the various commodities we purchase or produce, and foreign currency exchange and purchase contracts, as described below under </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#8220;Risk Management Activities by Type of Risk.&#8221;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> These derivative instruments are recorded as either assets or liabilities measured at their fair values (see </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;14</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">), as summarized below under </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#8220;Fair Values of Derivative Instruments.&#8221;</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> The effect of these derivative instruments on our income and other comprehensive income (loss) is summarized below under </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#8220;Effect of Derivative Instruments on Income and Other Comprehensive Income (Loss).&#8221;</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Risk Management Activities by Type of Risk</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Commodity Price Risk</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We are exposed to market risks related to the volatility in the price of crude oil, refined petroleum products (primarily gasoline and distillate),</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">renewable diesel, grain (primarily corn), renewable diesel feedstocks, and natural gas used in our operations. To reduce the impact of price volatility on our results of operations and cash flows, we use commodity derivative instruments, such as futures and options. Our positions in commodity derivative instruments are monitored and managed on a daily basis by our risk control group to ensure compliance with our stated risk management policy that has been approved by our board of directors.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We primarily use commodity derivative instruments as cash flow hedges and economic hedges. Our objectives for entering into each type of hedge is described below.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:48px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Cash flow hedges </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">&#8211; The objective of our cash flow hedges is to lock in the price of forecasted&#160;(i)&#160;feedstock, refined petroleum product, or natural gas purchases, or&#160;(ii)&#160;refined petroleum product or renewable diesel sales at existing market prices that we deem favorable.</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"><tr><td style="width:48px;"/><td/></tr><tr><td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:24px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">&#8226;</span></div></td><td style="vertical-align:top;"><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;">Economic hedges</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> &#8211; Our objectives for holding economic hedges are to&#160;(i)&#160;manage price volatility in certain feedstock and refined petroleum product inventories and fixed-price purchase contracts, and&#160;(ii)&#160;lock in the price of forecasted feedstock, refined petroleum product,</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ff0000;font-weight:bold;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">or natural gas purchases, or refined petroleum product or renewable diesel sales at existing market prices that we deem favorable.</span></div></td></tr></table><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;padding-left:48px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">As of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, we had the following outstanding commodity derivative instruments that were used as cash flow hedges and economic hedges, as well as commodity derivative instruments related to the physical purchase of corn at a fixed price. The information presents the notional volume of outstanding contracts by type of instrument and year of maturity (volumes in thousands of barrels, except corn contracts that are presented in thousands These contracts are not designated as hedging instruments for accounting purposes and therefore are classified as economic hedges. As of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, we had foreign currency contracts to purchase </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$220&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of U.S. dollars and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$2.5&#160;billion</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> of U.S. dollar equivalent Canadian dollars. Of these commitments, </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$1.2&#160;billion</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">matured on or before </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">April&#160;24, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and the remaining </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$1.5&#160;billion</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> will mature by </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">June&#160;15, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Environmental Compliance Program Price Risk</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We are exposed to market risk related to the volatility in the price of credits needed to comply with various governmental and regulatory environmental compliance programs. To manage this risk, we enter into contracts to purchase these credits when prices are deemed favorable. Some of these contracts are derivative instruments; however, we elect the normal purchase exception and do not record these contracts at their fair values. Certain of these programs require us to blend biofuels into the products we produce, and we are subject to such programs in most of the countries in which we operate. These countries set annual quotas for the percentage of biofuels that must be blended into the motor fuels consumed in these countries. As a producer of motor fuels from petroleum, we are obligated to blend biofuels into the products we produce at </span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">a rate that is at least equal to the applicable quota. To the degree we are unable to blend at the applicable rate, we must purchase biofuel credits (primarily RINs in the U.S.). We are exposed to the volatility in the market price of these credits, and we manage that risk by purchasing biofuel credits when prices are deemed favorable. The cost of meeting our obligations under these compliance programs was </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><span>$112&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;"><span>$91&#160;million</span></span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, respectively. These amounts are reflected in cost of materials and other.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We are subject to additional requirements under greenhouse gas (GHG) emission programs, including the cap-and-trade systems, as discussed in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">Note&#160;14</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. Under these cap-and-trade systems, we purchase various GHG emission credits available on the open market. Therefore, we are exposed to the volatility in the market price of these credits. The cost to implement certain provisions of the cap-and-trade systems are significant; however, we recovered the majority of these costs from our customers for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and expect to continue to recover the majority of these costs in the future. For the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the net cost of meeting our obligations under these compliance programs was immaterial.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Fair Values of Derivative Instruments</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The following tables provide information about the fair values of our derivative instruments as of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> and </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> (in&#160;millions) and the line items in the balance sheets in which the fair values are reflected. See </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">Note&#160;14</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> for additional information related to the fair values of our derivative instruments.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">As indicated in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#000000;text-decoration:none;">Note&#160;14</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, we net fair value amounts recognized for multiple similar derivative contracts executed with the same counterparty under master netting arrangements, including cash collateral assets and obligations. <td class="text"><div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:0px;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">1.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">BASIS OF PRESENTATION AND SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Basis of Presentation</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">General</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The terms &#8220;Valero,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221; and &#8220;us,&#8221; as used in this report, may refer to Valero Energy Corporation, one or more of its consolidated subsidiaries, or all of them taken as a whole.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">These unaudited financial statements have been prepared in accordance with United States (U.S.) generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) for interim financial information and with the instructions to Form&#160;10-Q and Article&#160;10 of Regulation&#160;S-X of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Accordingly, they do not include all of the information and notes required by U.S.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">GAAP for complete financial statements. In the opinion of management, all adjustments considered necessary for a fair presentation have been included. All such adjustments are of a normal recurring nature unless disclosed otherwise. Operating results for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be expected for the year ending </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">. As discussed in </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Note&#160;2</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">, the recent outbreak of COVID-19 and its development into a pandemic in March 2020 has resulted in significant economic disruption globally. This disruption became more acute in the latter half of March 2020; therefore, our operating results for the </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">three</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> months ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">March&#160;31, 2020</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> do not fully reflect the impact this disruption has had, and will likely continue to have, on us.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The balance sheet as of </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"> has been derived from our audited financial statements as of that date. For further information, refer to our financial statements and notes thereto included in our annual report on Form&#160;10-K for the year ended </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">December&#160;31, 2019</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Reclassifications</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">Prior year amounts for capital expenditures and repayments of debt and finance lease obligations in the consolidated statements of cash flows have been reclassified to conform to the 2020 presentation to separately provide these expenditures for us and our consolidated VIEs.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Significant Accounting Policies</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-indent:24px;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;">Use of Estimates</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S.</span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;"> </span><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">GAAP requires us to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes. Actual results could differ from those estimates. On an ongoing basis, we review our estimates based on currently available information. Changes in facts and circumstances may result in revised estimates.</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"><br/></span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Adoption of Accounting Pronouncements</span></div><div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"><span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;">We adopted the following Accounting Standards Updates (ASUs) on January&#160;1, 2020. We are actively responding to these matters on our business. We have reduced the amount of crude oil processed at most of our refineries in response to the decreased demand for our products, we have temporarily idled various gasoline-making units at certain of our refineries to further limit gasoline production, and we have taken measures to reduce jet fuel production. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;Eight&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of our ethanol plants are temporarily idled, and we reduced the amount of ethanol produced at our remaining &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; ethanol plants to address the decreased demand for ethanol.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:14px;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Many uncertainties remain with respect to COVID-19, including its resulting economic effects, and we are unable to predict the ultimate economic impacts from COVID-19 on our business and how quickly national economies can recover once the pandemic subsides. However, the adverse impacts of the economic effects from COVID-19 and uncertainty in the global oil markets on our business have been and will likely continue to be significant. As a result, we expect these matters may affect our estimates and assumptions on amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes in the near term.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Impairment Analysis of Long-Lived Assets&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Due to the adverse economic conditions discussed above, we reviewed our significant operating assets for the existence of impairment indicators. As a result of this review, we evaluated &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;six&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;ethanol plants for potential impairment as of March&#160;31, 2020, assuming that we would operate these plants in the future and incorporating current price assumptions into our future estimated cash flows. Based on our analysis, we determined that &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;the carrying amount of each of these plants was recoverable, as the undiscounted future cash flows from each plant exceeded its respective carrying value. Nonetheless, we will continue to evaluate the economic conditions and their impact on our assumptions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Impairment Analysis of Goodwill&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We have &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$260&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; of goodwill as of March&#160;31, 2020. All of our goodwill is allocated to one reporting unit, the U.S. Gulf Coast refining region. Our annual test for the impairment of goodwill is performed on October&#160;1 of each year. However, as discussed above, there were adverse changes in the capital and commodity markets that contributed to a significant decline in our common stock price. Despite the decline in our common stock price, we determined our goodwill was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;t impaired.       id="TextSelection-77972EF1F3FF5FD7ADFA8B5121B8D10D-0-wk-Fact-ECE4B2053BC0591F91A7F8E5A3F8289D">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:11pt;padding-left:0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;3.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;MERGER WITH VLP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;On January&#160;10, 2019, we completed our acquisition of all of the outstanding publicly held common units of VLP pursuant to a definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger (Merger Agreement, and together with the transactions contemplated thereby, the Merger Transaction) with VLP. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, each outstanding publicly held common unit was converted into the right to receive &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$42.25&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&#160;per common unit in cash without any interest thereon, and all such publicly traded common units were automatically canceled and ceased to exist. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, we paid aggregate merger consideration of&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;color:#ee2724;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$950&#160;million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;, which was funded with available cash on hand.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;Prior to the completion of the Merger Transaction, we consolidated the financial statements of VLP and reflected noncontrolling interests on our balance sheet for the portion of VLP&#x2019;s partners&#x2019; capital held by VLP&#x2019;s public common unitholders. Upon completion of the Merger Transaction, VLP became our indirect wholly owned subsidiary and, as a result, we no longer reflect noncontrolling interests on our balance sheet with respect to VLP. In addition, we no longer attribute a portion of VLP&#x2019;s net income to noncontrolling interests. Because we had a controlling financial interest in VLP before the Merger Transaction and retained our controlling financial interest in VLP after the Merger Transaction, the change in our ownership interest in VLP as a result of the merger was accounted for as an equity transaction. Accordingly, we did not recognize a gain or loss on the Merger Transaction.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:BusinessCombinationDisclosureTextBlock>

style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;7,013&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:bottom;border-bottom:3px double #000000;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We compare the market value of inventories to their cost on an aggregate basis, excluding materials and supplies. In determining the market value of our inventories, we assume that feedstocks are converted into refined products, which requires us to make estimates regarding the refined products expected to be produced from those feedstocks and the conversion costs required to convert those feedstocks into refined products. We also estimate the usual and customary transportation costs required to move the inventory from our plants to the appropriate points of sale. We then apply an estimated selling price to our inventories. If the aggregate market value is less than the aggregate cost, we recognize a loss for the difference in our statements of income. However, to the extent the aggregate market value subsequently increases, we would recognize an increase to the value of our inventories (not to exceed cost) and a gain in our statements of income.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;The market value of our last-in, first-out (LIFO) inventory as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; fell below our historical LIFO inventory costs. As a result, we recorded an LCM inventory valuation adjustment of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.5&#160;billion&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; for the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt; months ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;March&#160;31, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;. The income statement effect differs from the balance sheet reserve due to the foreign currency effect of inventories held for our international operations.       id="TextSelection-CD362C28F1D551A5BD882AE89DED9661-0-wk-Fact-58612B0572D151598E0FCF63A45E6A5A">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:justify;font-size:11pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:11pt;"&gt;We hold variable interests in VIEs that have not been consolidated because we are not considered the primary beneficiary. These non-consolidated VIEs are not material to our financial position or results of operations and are accounted for as equity investments.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;We consolidate a VIE when we have a variable interest in an entity for which we are the primary beneficiary.</us-gaap:ConsolidationVariableInterestEntityPolicy>
